clean_body: Session is over. We did a lot of good, we stopped a lot of bad. | | | | | | | Capitol Report May 13, 2022 | | Sen. Steven Roberts, D-St. Louis discusses the end-of-session victories this week: $19 million secured for the 5th district, LRA passage, and the defeat of Republican efforts to undermine the initiative petition process. | | Contact Senator Roberts 201 W. Capitol Ave., Rm 329 Jefferson City, MO 65101 (573) 751-4415 Steve.Roberts@senate.mo.gov | | | | | | | | | | | | SENATOR FINALIZES NEW CONGRESSIONAL REDISTRICTING PLAN The Senate on May 12 voted 22-11 to grant send a congressional redistricting plan to the governor and then abruptly called it quits for the year a day ahead of the constitutional adjournment deadline. The late-session action allows Missouri to have new congressional districts in place for the Aug. 2 primary election. A small group of hardline conservative Republicans had blocked Senate action on redistricting all year amid demands for an aggressive gerrymander that would give the GOP a 7-1 advantage in Missouri’s congressional delegation. Most majority Republicans, however, favored maintaining the 6-2 status quo that has been in place for the last decade. Democrats argued that the status quo is itself a gerrymander and that based on the state’s political performance in congressional elections, Missouri should have a 5-3 map. With a House-approved redistricting bill stuck in committee, Senate Republican leadership invoked a rarely used constitutional procedure to bring the bill directly the chamber for debate. Although the hardliners decried the move as a “sneak attack,” they ultimately didn’t block a final vote. Since the Senate made no changes to the bill, which the House approved days earlier on a 97-47 vote, it goes straight to governor, who is expected to sign it into law. The legislature had to redraw the state’s congressional map to reflect population shifts under the 2020 U.S. Census. But since a new plan wasn’t in place when the candidate filing period ended in March, candidates filed under the outdated congressional map adopted in 2011, sparking at least three lawsuits in state and federal courts seeking to block its use. If lawmakers had failed to enact a redistricting plan, the task would have fallen to a three-judge panel of federal judges. | | INITIATIVE PETITIONS FILED ON LEGAL MARIJUANA, RANKED-CHOICE VOTING Supporters of separate initiative petitions to legalize recreational marijuana in Missouri and create a system of ranked-choice voting for state and federal elections turned in signatures by the May 8 deadline in hopes of getting their proposals on the Nov. 8 statewide ballot. The Missouri Secretary of State’s Office must now verify that each petition has sufficient signatures to go before voters. The initiative process allows voters to bypass the General Assembly to independently propose and enact legislation. Putting a proposed constitutional amendment on the ballot requires a minimum of about 172,000 signatures from registered Missouri voters. According to The Associated Press, supporters of the marijuana initiative said they collected more than 385,000 signatures, while backers of the elections proposal touted gathering more than 300,000 signatures. The recreational marijuana measure follows up on a successful 2019 initiative petition that legalized pot for medical use. In addition to legalizing recreational marijuana use for those age 21 and over, it also would automatically expunge past convictions for marijuana-related crimes – other than driving under the influence – for non-violent offenders. Under the elections initiative, candidates for the state legislature, statewide executive branch office or Congress would appear on the same primary ballot without regard to party, with the top four candidates advancing to the general election. During that election, voters could vote for multiple candidates, ranking who they like best in order of preference. If no candidate received a majority on the first tabulation, the candidate with the fewest votes would be eliminated and their votes redistributed among the other candidates based on each voter’s preference. That process would continue until a winner emerged. The signature verification process typically takes months, but there is an expedited process the secretary of state can use to get it done it couple weeks. If that process is used, it’s possible the petitions could be verified in time for the governor to exercise his authority to move one or both measures to the Aug. 2 primary ballot. | | 2022 SENATE BILLS \- Modifies provisions relating to parole eligibility \- Authorizes a property tax credit for certain senior citizens \- Creates new provisions relating to financial institutions \- Modifies the practice of dentistry to include the prescription and administration of vaccines \- Modifies the Show-Me Heroes Program to provide for grants for veteran apprenticeship training programs \- Modifies provisions relating to the offense of unlawful use of weapons \- Relating to the legal minimum standard for valuation of insurance policies and contracts \- Creates provisions relating to certificates of moral character for persons convicted of certain offenses \- Modifies provisions relating to travel insurance \- Modifies provisions relating to arrests by private persons \- Modifies provisions relating to wrongful convictions \- Authorizes a tax credit for employers providing educational assistance to employees \- Establishes provisions relating to inquiries of wage ranges \- Establishes provisions relating to alternative dispute resolution processes \- Creates provisions relating to grants to not-for-profit organizations for physical security measures \- Designates "Police Officer Tamarris Bohannon Memorial Bridge" \- Modifies provisions relating to the Municipal Land Reutilization Law - body:
#
Happy (?) Friday the 13th, Derek.
You won’t catch me getting scared by superstition or Jason Voorhees today, because what I’m afraid of is a heck of a lot scarier than some dude in a mask.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220513-2?refcode=em20220513-5811&refcode2=5811_434096_i0EHdz&akid=5811%2E434096%2Ei0EHdz)
**The GOP keeping this Senate seat red is most definitely the scariest thing I can think of.**
From the urgent need to defend abortion access across the country to the millions of minimum wage workers who desperately deserve a raise, **we cannot afford to let the GOP keep this seat + gain a Senate majority.**
[**That’s why I’m asking if you, Derek, can chip in $13 to help us carry our momentum through next Tuesday’s primary and beyond. Every dollar you chip in will make a huge difference in this race.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220513-2?amount=13&refcode=em20220513-5811&refcode2=5811_434096_i0EHdz&akid=5811%2E434096%2Ei0EHdz)
You know what else is weird? Imagine a world where a celebrity TV doctor or a former hedge fund CEO represents the great Commonwealth of Pennsylvania in the Senate.
Dr. Oz + David McCormick not only have terrible political views, but they also are endorsed by other pretty terrible dudes (Dr. Oz + Donald Trump, Ted Cruz + David McCormick).
Also...I never thought this would be a flex, but __I ACTUALLY LIVE IN PENNSYLVANIA!!!
Finally, Derek, these GOP boogeymen are far scarier to me than any bad luck or movie villains, because, if given the power, they could permanently screw over working people + families across this country.
We, the people, have the power to not let that happen. We just need to work together and push through these last few days leading up to the primary.
**[So, what do you say? Can you make a donation of $13, or whatever you can afford, to help us win this primary so we can go on to flip this seat blue in November?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220513-2?amount=13&refcode=em20220513-5811&refcode2=5811_434096_i0EHdz&akid=5811%2E434096%2Ei0EHdz)**
**[Donate $13 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20220513-2?amount=13&refcode=em20220513-5811&refcode2=5811_434096_i0EHdz&akid=5811%2E434096%2Ei0EHdz)**
Your support will forever + always mean the world to me + my team. 🙏
John
John Fetterman
Lt. Governor of Pennsylvania

**Congressman Dan Meuser endorses Barletta for Governor**
---
Former mayor and congressman Lou Barletta, leading Republican candidate for governor of Pennsylvania, today announced the formal endorsement of Congressman Dan Meuser (PA-09). Meuser is the latest in a growing number of key endorsements coalescing behind Barletta's campaign over the last 48 hours including: Senate Pro Tempore and former gubernatorial candidate Jake Corman, former Congresswoman and gubernatorial candidate Melissa Hart, Congressman Fred Keller, former US Senator Rick Santorum, former governor Mark Schweiker, former Lt. Governor Jim Cawley, Senate Majority Whip John Gordner, Senator Tommy Tomlinson, Senator Bob Mensch, Senator John DiSanto, Representative Kurt Masser, and Representative Doyle Heffley, amongst others.

“We’ve all seen the mess that Gov. Wolf created and we know that Josh Shapiro would certainly make it worse,” said **Congressman Dan Meuser**. “We have a chance as Republicans to correct course and accomplish great things for the people of Pennsylvania, but only if we nominate a candidate for governor who can win in November. Lou loves Pennsylvania and is the only candidate who has a plan for what Pennsylvania can be. I am pleased to endorse Lou Barletta, who is the one Republican who can unite the party and bring home victory in the fall.”

clean_body: | | | | Look what he just killed. | Peter, At a time when gas prices are at record highs in the United States, crippling our workers and families, Joe Biden and Deb Haaland are canceling more oil leases, right here in Alaska. To make matters worse, Liberal Lisa Murkowski was the tie-breaking vote to advance the confirmation of Interior Secretary Deb Haaland, who brought this disastrous decision down, killing Alaskan jobs and energy. This decision shows a reckless apathy for Americans and Alaskans. When oil isn't flowing, our dads can't provide for their families, our moms can't feed their children, and across the nation, workers can't fill up their cars to get to work. Over 1 million acres here in Alaska’s Cook Inlet have the potential to unleash American energy, but under this energy-annihilating Administration, we're out of business. When I am elected, I will fight to unleash Alaskan and American energy and bring down costs at the pump. We will use our God-given resources to create jobs and make America Energy Independent Again. | | | | | Thank you, | | Kelly Tshibaka | STAY UP TO DATE WITH KELLY AND THE CAMPAIGN BY CLICKING THIS LINK: "ckq.io/yl3xzs" | | | | =
